newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bankruptcy debt drops 35.4 pct in Aug yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Japan bankruptcy debt drops 35.4 pct in Aug yr/yr.

text.p: Total debt held by bankrupt firms in Japan in August dropped 35.4 percent from the same month a year ago to 529.4 billion yen, a private research and rating company said on Friday.

But despite the fall in August, the situation for some firms has not shown shown a drastic improvement due to Japan's fuzzy economic recovery, Tokyo Commerce and Industry Research Co said in a report.
"The economic situation is so bleary and unclear that small and mid-sized companies are still facing a lot of pressure," Tokyo Commerce said.
Bankruptcy debt in August fell 20.7 percent from July.
Bankruptcies are defined as insolvent companies in the process of liquidation or reorganisation under court protection from creditors.
There were 1,128 business failures in August, down 19.8 percent year on year, and down 8.8 percent from July.
There were 52 cases of bankruptcies with debts amounting to more than one billion yen. There were five cases with debts of more than 10 billion yen, compared to nine a year earlier.
The figures indicate that bankruptcies due to debts hanging over from the bursting of the "bubble" economy in the early 1990s have fallen off, the research institute said.
Sales difficulties, including rising debts and trouble collecting money owed, were blamed for 58.4 percent, or 659, of the bankruptcies reported in August.

Bankruptcy figures were lower compared to a year earlier in all industries. The 1,128 business failures included 308 bankruptcy cases in the construction industry, down 19.7 percent from the year ago, and 230 cases in the manufacturing industry, down 31.3 percent.
In the wholesale sector, there were 226 cases, down 3.4 percent from the year ago, and 128 cases in the retail industry, down 32.2 percent.
